lines.t: Stone walls built on shifting ground,
Voices echo, but truth’s drowned out.
Altars burn with borrowed light,
They preach the day but fear the night.
Hands raised high but hearts grow cold,
Silver crowns, these thrones of gold.
The sacred words are dressed in pride,
While the humble truth waits outside.
In the churches of men, the towers sway,
They call to heaven but fade away.
Paper saints in stained disguise,
Lose their soul beneath the lies.
In the churches of men, we break and bend,
But love was meant to have no end.
Empty prayers through iron skies,
Faith for sale where mercy dies.
A voice still calls beyond the noise,
The Shepherd cries, “Hear My voice.”
The stones will crack, the veils will tear,
The Truth returns to clear the air.
No crowned deceit, no temple flame,
Just love that burns without a name.
In the churches of men, the towers sway,
They call to heaven but fade away.
Paper saints in stained disguise,
Lose their soul beneath the lies.
In the churches of men, we break and bend,
But love was meant to have no end.
Light falls through broken glass,
Revealing all we tried to mask.
The walls collapse, the voices fade,
Only truth remains unafraid.
No preacher stands, no choir sings,
Just freedom beating, broken wings.
In the churches of men, the towers fall,
But through the ruin, You still call.
No gold, no name, no crowns remain,
Only love beyond the pain.
In the ashes, we begin again,
Far from the churches of men.
